signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: The G10 currency scorecard shows JPY leading all peers with a 1W average of +2.334% across 7 pairs, while NZD lags at -1.408% across 4 pairs, creating a 3.742% spread that breaches the critical threshold. Heightened tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and tanker disruption headlines drive broad demand into JPY despite its carry disadvantage, where RBNZ at 2.75% vs BoJ at 1.0% leaves a 175bp nominal carry gap favoring NZD. CFTC positioning shows NZD leveraged funds net short -23,004 contracts at the 4th percentile (z -1.81), reflecting an established institutional short that is accelerating downside momentum. Spot NZD/USD trades at 0.5884, slipping below its SMA20 at 0.5910 while holding above the SMA50/200 cluster around 0.5839/0.5855. JPY strength dominates cross flows as long as maritime transit concerns in the Persian Gulf keep commodity risk premiums elevated. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY; cross-asset tension overrides the nominal carry advantage. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias in focus. Risk: Persian Gulf shipping tensions de-escalate swiftly, prompting immediate carry-trade re-engagement.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Crowded Short Squeeze
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 156.16, breaking decisively below its SMA20 (158.96), SMA50 (160.48), and SMA200 (158.45) daily moving average cluster. The Saxo 25-delta risk reversal sits at -2.54, reflecting aggressive downside put protection demand that contradicts the prevailing CFTC speculative positioning. Leveraged funds hold JPY net short -111,297 contracts at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range (z -2.18), with net positioning expanding by -29,678 contracts on the week. Although SOFR at 3.66% vs TONA at 0.98% maintains a +268bp carry advantage for the dollar, mounting BoJ hawkish commentary alongside Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks is forcing leveraged shorts to cover. The extreme put skew confirms institutional options desks are pricing accelerated downside volatility despite low headline VIX at 14.5. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, asymmetric squeeze on crowded speculative carry shorts. Catalyst: US August CPI release on 11 Sep. Risk: Fed reiterates a prolonged hold at 3.75% while BoJ leaves policy unadjusted on 18 Sep, restoring carry support toward 158.45.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Retail Sentiment Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7210, maintaining an intact bullish technical posture above its SMA20 (0.7135), SMA50 (0.7041), and SMA200 (0.6988). CFTC data shows leveraged funds holding AUD net long +50,250 contracts, sitting at the 94th percentile of the 52-week distribution (z +1.79), indicating stretched speculative participation. Conversely, Myfxbook retail sentiment registers an extreme 90% short position against 10% long, establishing a stark institutional-versus-retail divergence. AONIA at 4.35% vs SOFR at 3.66% delivers a 69bp carry advantage to AUD, supporting the spot uptrend alongside WTI crude holding at $91.5 on Hormuz supply friction. However, weekly leveraged fund net buying contracted by 3,328 contracts, signaling late-trend positioning saturation where additional upside requires fresh fundamental sponsorship. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; institutional trend remains dominant despite crowded positioning. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — 4.35% policy hold expected. Risk: A sharp drop in crude and commodity prices undermines terms of trade, triggering leveraged long liquidation below 0.7135.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Volatility Risk Premium + Policy Parity
signals.text: GBP/USD sits at 1.3519, holding below its SMA20 at 1.3555 while remaining supported above the SMA50 at 1.3456 and SMA200 at 1.3447. Implied volatility on 1-month options runs at 11.0% against a 30-day realized volatility of 4.7%, generating a substantial +6.3% volatility risk premium. Leveraged speculative positioning is stretched at +47,504 contracts net long (93rd percentile, z +1.27), although funds reduced exposure by 9,335 contracts in the latest reporting week. SONIA at 3.73% vs SOFR at 3.66% leaves a negligible 7bp spread, while the Fed at 3.75% and BoE at 3.75% provide 0bp of policy rate carry advantage. Disappointing UK macroeconomic surprises with an ESI of -6.7 and elevated options hedging demand suggest investors are paying up for tail protection ahead of central bank decisions. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD, elevated volatility premium and stalling institutional net inflows constrain directional extension. Catalyst: BoE policy meeting 17 Sep. Risk: US CPI surprises substantially to the downside, reigniting dollar liquidation toward 1.3600.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Implied Volatility Premium + Restrictive Spread
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1618, consolidating between its SMA20 at 1.1611 and SMA200 at 1.1638, with the SMA50 positioned below at 1.1512. Implied volatility stands at 7.1% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.7%, reflecting a notable +2.4% volatility risk premium that indicates persistent hedging activity over spot price movement. Institutional rate dynamics structurally favor the greenback, with SOFR at 3.66% vs €STR at 2.19% yielding a +147bp carry advantage, backed by Fed 3.75% vs ECB 2.4% establishing a 135bp policy rate gap. CFTC leveraged funds hold EUR net short -52,784 contracts (31st percentile), showing moderate net-short positioning that has absorbed modest weekly buying of 2,527 contracts. The 25-delta risk reversal sits near flat at -0.22, confirming that institutional options demand is focused on tail volatility rather than directional asymmetry. Trade bias: Neutral/range EUR/USD; carry advantage for USD counters near-term range support. Catalyst: ECB rate decision 10 Sep. Risk: ECB delivers an unexpectedly hawkish policy guidance update, compressing the nominal rate differential.
